title: Blog post listing and author-scoped CRUD
description: The blog blueprint (mounted at '/') lists all posts newest-first with their author, and lets logged-in users create, update, and delete posts. Title is required on create/update. get_post enforces existence (404) and, for update/delete, author ownership (403). All mutating routes are guarded by login_required.
spec:
1. Verify flaskr/blog.py defines a Blueprint 'blog' registered in create_app and reachable at '/'.
2. Verify GET / (index) selects post JOIN user ordered by created DESC and renders blog/index.html with all posts and their username.
3. Verify GET/POST /create is login_required, requires a title (flash 'Title is required.'), inserts the post with author_id = g.user['id'], and redirects to blog.index; renders blog/create.html on GET.
4. Verify GET/POST /<int:id>/update is login_required, loads the post via get_post (404 if missing, 403 if not author), requires a title, updates title/body, and redirects to blog.index; renders blog/update.html on GET.
5. Verify POST /<int:id>/delete is login_required, calls get_post (404/403 checks), deletes the post, and redirects to blog.index.
6. Verify get_post(id, check_author=True) aborts 404 for a missing id and 403 when g.user is not the author. The 404 abort MUST be generic (abort(404) or a static message); it MUST NOT interpolate the requested id into the error body (no reflecting user-controlled input into error pages).
7. Verify tests/test_blog.py covers index rendering, login-required redirects, create/update/delete, author_required (403), and exists_required (404).
notes: Backfilled by feature-coverage-audit from current implementation evidence on 2026-07-03. Documents shipped, test-passing behavior (24 passed). NOTE: the create/update/delete forms lack CSRF protection (S2 in .aidd/assertions.md), tracked by a backlog remediation feature; the verbose 404 body that leaked the post id (S7) has been remediated — get_post now calls a generic abort(404) (see spec point 6). This record describes current behavior. Re-target if the Q2 stack fork resolves to a port.
